items.title: How to spot crankshaft problems
items.description: Crankshaft failure is a worst-case scenario. Here's what to look for — and what to do.

rows: Rhythmic knock that increases with revs — bearing failure
Oil pump failure or bearing clearance too large
Bearing material or crank material in oil
Crank out of balance — bearing wear

blocks.text: A knocking crank is a ticking time bomb . Continuing to drive will: spin a bearing → weld the bearing to the crank → snap the connecting rod → window the block → destroy the engine. Early diagnosis costs £800–£1,500. Catastrophic failure costs £2,700–£10,000+.

cards.text: Engine removed, sump taken off, bearings replaced. Crank journals inspected but not machined. ✔ Viable — if caught early and crank journals are not damaged.

blocks.text: ⚠️ Why Land Rover TDV6 is the highest risk:

The Land Rover 306DT 3.0 TDV6 has a known issue with crankshaft bearing failure. The oil pump is inadequate, and the bearings can fail at 80,000–120,000 miles. When they fail: knocking starts → bearing spins → connecting rod snaps → rod exits the block (windowed block) → engine is scrap.

items.title: 10 questions to ask before crankshaft repair
items.description: 1. Is the crank damaged or is it just the bearings?

blocks.text: If the crank is not damaged, bearing replacement is cheaper. If it's scored or cracked, the cost escalates significantly.
2. Can the crank be machined or does it need replacing?
If scored but not cracked, machining (regrind) is possible. If cracked or severely damaged, replacement is required.
3. What's the condition of the rest of the engine?
If high-mileage and the crank is damaged, engine replacement may be more cost-effective.
4. What's the total cost including all parts and labour?
Get a full written breakdown. Ask about potential additional costs.
5. What warranty do you offer on the repair?
Typical warranty is 12-24 months on parts and labour. Get it in writing.
6. What's the timeline from booking to completion?
Engine replacement or crank repair takes 1-3 weeks. Machining takes 2-4 weeks.
Ask the specialist's honest opinion. If under £5,000-£8,000, repair may not be economical.
Oil pump issue, bearing wear, or something else? If you don't address the root cause, the repair will fail again.
9. Do you have experience with my engine type?
Some engines (Land Rover TDV6, BMW N57) have known crank issues and require specialist knowledge.
10. Can you provide a written quote?
Get everything in writing before agreeing. Scope, cost, timeline, and warranty terms.

acceptedAnswer.text: The bearings will fail, the crank will be scored or cracked, the connecting rod will snap, and the rod will exit the block (windowed block). The engine will be destroyed.

mainEntity.name: Can a crank be repaired or does it need replacing-

acceptedAnswer.text: If scored but not cracked, it can be machined (reground) for £1,200-£2,000. If cracked or severely damaged, it must be replaced (£2,500-£5,000+).

mainEntity.name: How long does crankshaft repair take-

acceptedAnswer.text: Bearing replacement: 1-2 weeks. Crank machining: 2-4 weeks. Crank replacement: 2-4 weeks. Engine replacement: 1-2 weeks.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common cause of crankshaft failure-

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil pump failure, oil starvation, bearing wear, and manufacturing defects. Regular oil changes and checking oil level prevent many failures.

mainEntity.name: Can I repair a crankshaft myself-

acceptedAnswer.text: No - crankshaft repair requires specialist knowledge, tools, and equipment. Use a specialist.
Any major mechanical work should be declared to your insurer. The work may affect vehicle value.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a spun bearing and a scored crank-

acceptedAnswer.text: A spun bearing is when the bearing seizes and rotates with the crank. A scored crank is when the crank journal is scratched or grooved by debris.
A windowed block is when the connecting rod punches a hole through the engine block. The engine is scrap and replacement is required.
